laws.rule: Northern Ireland councils make bye-laws banning drinking alcohol in designated streets and public open spaces. In Causeway Coast and Glens (which includes the Giant's Causeway coast), drinking in a designated place is an offence with a fine of up to GBP 500 (about A$951, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) on conviction.
laws.heading: Consumption of Intoxicating Liquor in Designated Places bye-laws

laws.rule: Northern Ireland licensed premises may sell and serve alcohol only during permitted hours, and selling, buying, consuming or taking away alcohol outside them is an offence (Licensing (Northern Ireland) Order 1996, art 41). The general permitted hours (art 42(1)) are 11:30 am to 11 pm Monday to Saturday, 12:30 pm to 11 pm on Sundays, and 12:30 pm to 10 pm on Christmas Day. Off-licences (premises selling only for drinking elsewhere) have their own hours of 8 am to 11 pm on weekdays and 10 am to 10 pm on Sundays, and none on Christmas Day (art 42(2)). Extra hours can be granted for particular premises or events (arts 44 to 49), so a venue's licence may differ.
laws.heading: Licensing (Northern Ireland) Order 1996, arts 41 and 42

laws.rule: It is an offence to smoke in a smoke-free private vehicle in Northern Ireland. A private vehicle is smoke-free when it is enclosed, has more than one person in it and has someone under 18 in it. Windows down or doors open does not stop it being enclosed. The rule does not cover motorcycles or convertibles with the roof fully down, and caravans and motor homes are covered only when on the road.
laws.heading: Smoke-free regulations (Northern Ireland), as summarised by nidirect

laws.rule: Since 1 June 2025 it is an offence in Northern Ireland to supply, offer to supply or hold for supply a single-use vape (a vape not designed to be reused). On conviction in the magistrates' court the penalty is a fine up to the statutory maximum; on conviction on indictment it is up to 2 years in prison, a fine or both (Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2024, regs 1, 3 and 4, as amended from 29 July 2025). The offence is aimed at suppliers, not at a visitor using a vape. nidirect also says retailers may not sell any vaping product, including non-nicotine vapes, to anyone under 18.
laws.heading: Environmental Protection (Single-use Vapes) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2024, regs 1, 3, 4

laws.rule: In Northern Ireland the possession, purchase, sale, acquisition, handling or use of fireworks is prohibited except under a licence (Explosives (Fireworks) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2002, reg 4(1); the licence process is in reg 6). Schedule 1 lists fireworks exempt from that prohibition. This is a different system from the hours-based rules in England, Wales and Scotland.
laws.heading: Explosives (Fireworks) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2002, regs 4, 6 and Schedule 1

laws.rule: Northern Ireland's drink-driving limit is 35 micrograms of alcohol per 100 ml of breath, 80 mg per 100 ml of blood or 107 mg per 100 ml of urine. Scotland's limit is lower (50 mg per 100 ml of blood). Penalties depend on the circumstances of the case.
